headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from AutoGPT feeding unstructured document outputs into a writable, networked pipeline; no direct evidence of a shared channel beyond filesystem/API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while unstructured processes documents and exposes file-based outputs. If unstructured emits attacker-controlled text that AutoGPT treats as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default file-based workflows. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF unstructured writes attacker-controlled document text into a shared directory that AutoGPT later ingests
IF AutoGPT treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate input and instruction directories
Add a provenance header check before AutoGPT reads files
Require manual review of extracted text before agent ingestion
Use read-only mounts for unstructured outputs
requires-engineering: implement content-signing or metadata tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, so sensitive documents processed by unstructured could be read by AutoGPT and then forwarded in its context or outputs. No secrets or PHI are explicitly listed, but the shared file surface plus networked inference path makes leakage plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared workspace
IF AutoGPT forwards extracted content to external APIs or logs
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside the shared workspace
Disable network egress for one agent during processing
Redact documents before unstructured ingests them
Review logs for document text leakage
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write via shell/subprocesses and unstructured can read/write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. They do not both advertise unrestricted write to the same directory, but overlapping mutable file access is plausible and could cause clobbering or race conditions. Unstructured supports multiple instances, while AutoGPT does not, increasing coordination risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF AutoGPT and unstructured modify the same filenames or manifests without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run only one writer at a time
Make unstructured outputs append-only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured produces extracted text and documents, and AutoGPT can consume filesystem content and act through shell/subprocesses. If AutoGPT treats unstructured output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. The pair has no documented verification step, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT uses unstructured output as input without human verification
IF downstream actions are triggered from extracted text or metadata
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actioning outputs
Require confidence thresholds on extracted fields
Compare extracted text against source documents
Limit AutoGPT to drafting, not executing, actions
requires-engineering: add validation and rollback gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list only generic document/text handling with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The only compliance concern visible is that unstructured’s privacy-policy endpoint and document processing could differ from AutoGPT’s unspecified handling, but the profiles do not show a concrete violation. I therefore keep this low.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated documents through unstructured without a matching policy
IF retention or residency settings differ between the two agents
mitigations: Review privacy policy and retention settings
Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed
Document the data flow for both agents
Restrict processing to non-sensitive documents
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across the pipeline
